decisions.reason: Having remained a clearly articulated product line tied to the firm's core geospatial integration capabilities, it likely meets or is close enough to aspiration levels to justify retention.

The building data digital twin service is still somewhat demand-uncertain, but its continued presence and strong fit with the firm's strategic direction make continued trial and refinement more likely than withdrawal.

As a close complement to enterprise GeoIT solutions, the authentication and identity delegation service would likely be kept unless its results fall distinctly below aspirations or are absorbed by overlapping offerings.
The open GIS application development framework supports the firm's platform-oriented, customizable solution model, so management would be reluctant to drop it absent clear underperformance.

The GIS-specific identity and access service appears strategically useful and still young enough that, with no clear failure signal, the firm would likely continue it while monitoring whether it outperforms alternative identity offerings.

The consulting workshop builds directly on the firm's established advisory business and likely requires limited dedicated assets, so organizational slack and strategic fit favor keeping it while market response develops.
